description: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of topics or domains evaluated in the context of automatic attribution evaluation for large language models, as referenced in the paper “Automatic Evaluation of Attribution by Large Language Models.” The chart is divided into eleven distinct segments, each labeled with a topic category and its corresponding percentage. The largest segment is “AI/NLP Research” at 24.3%, followed by “Econ. & Fin.” at 18.4%. Other notable segments include “History” and “Game&Anime,” both at 8.2%; “Daily Life” at 7.1%; “Med & Health” and “Science,” both at 6.7%; “Pet & Animal” at 5.5%; “Business” at 5.9%; “Law” at 5.1%; “Geography” at 2.7%; and “Math,” the smallest segment, at 1.2%. Each slice is color-coded and connected to its label via a thin line, with percentages displayed adjacent to the labels. The segments are arranged in a roughly descending order clockwise from the top right, though not strictly sorted. No slice is visually exploded or emphasized beyond its proportional size, and the chart uses a muted, desaturated color palette for all segments.
